title: Harbor Entrance Bell
narration: Cast in 1891, this bell greeted ferries before the museum occupied the pier. Conservators left the shallow crack visible so visitors can see how often the bell was struck during fog. The tone you hear today is slightly lower than the original because decades of salt air softened the bronze.

title: Mapmaker's Desk
narration: This writing desk belonged to a surveyor who charted the estuary by hand. The drawers are lined with wax to protect paper from damp air, and the pale rings on the surface were left by compasses rather than coffee cups. Every tool faces outward so it could be grabbed quickly on a moving boat.

title: Storm Glass Wall
narration: These cloudy cylinders are storm glasses once carried by captains who hoped crystal patterns could hint at incoming weather. The museum does not present them as reliable forecasts. Instead, this stop shows how sailors mixed folklore, experiment, and repeated observation when the horizon offered only partial evidence.

title: Restoration Window
narration: Behind the glass, technicians are cleaning a painted figurehead recovered from a warehouse fire. The missing color on the shoulder has not been repainted yet. The museum keeps that scar visible so visitors can compare original pigment, soot damage, and the reversible materials used in modern restoration.
